newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher - Buba stance can maybe block Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher - Buba stance can maybe block Bonn.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Thursday the German central bank's strong rejection of Bonn's intentions to revalue its reserves may be enough to block a legal change in parliament.
"I believe the statement by the Bundesbank may be sufficient to block a change in the law," Kuehbacher told journalists in Berlin.

The Bonn government is pushing ahead with its plan to introduce legislation in parliament to alter the Bundesbank law in a bid to unlock billions of marks in hidden reserves in gold and foreign exchange holdings.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday he would still go forward with the law change even though the Bundesbank strongly rejected Waigel's plan that asks for part of the profit booked on the reserves be transferred this year to Bonn.
The move to revalue the reserves is part of Bonn's attempts to whip its finances into shape to meet entry criteria for the new currency slated to begin on January 1, 1999.
Kuehbacher, a member of the opposition Social Democratic Party (SPD), said the move would carry a "stigma" and would hurt confidence in the new currency.

Kuehbacher, who is president of the regional state central bank of Berlin and Brandenberg, said he saw no signals that Bonn plans to step down from the proposed law change that would revalue gold and currency holdings nearer to market prices.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer will outline the central bank's stance at a parliament committee hearing on Thursday, Kuehbacher said.
He also "completely ruled out" that Tietmeyer would resign.
The Bundesbank on Wednesday rejected market rumours that Tietmeyer planned to quit.
